vuln_id: OSS-Fuzz issue 42470395 / ARVO arvo:42470395 / HarfBuzz dfont resourcesZ neuter to EOF face

project.name: HarfBuzz
project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable checkout that reproduced the saved ASan crash is `_work/src/harfbuzz` at `ca746f261e1e54cec2f9c8bc7a6f930491e19418`, a later vulnerable state than metadata commit `01b9148d9ae7d18228538774243e49840cfd2499`. Diffing the relevant files shows only a local `type_base` refactor in `ResourceMap::sanitize`; the null-enabled dfont offset declarations and the crashing line numbers used here are unchanged.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42470395 (harfbuzz): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target hb-shape-fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42470395
bug_description.original_source: ARVO-Meta / OSS-Fuzz report / staged vulnerable source / staged patch.diff / staged sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 256-byte witness begins with `0x00000100`, so HarfBuzz sanitizes it as a dfont `ResourceForkHeader` rather than as an ordinary sfnt. Static decoding of that same witness shows `map=1`, `data=256`, `dataLen=0`, `typeList=14`, and the first resource-type record `tag='sfnt'`, `resCountM1=129`, `resourcesZ=44`. Validating that type's resource array should fail, because `type_base + resourcesZ` is absolute file offset 59 and only 197 bytes remain there, while `resCountM1 + 1` promises 130 `ResourceRecord`s (`1560` bytes). In the vulnerable source, however, `ResourceTypeRecord.resourcesZ` is a null-enabled `OffsetTo`, so `OffsetTo::sanitize()` neuters the field to `0` instead of rejecting the malformed dfont when deep validation fails. Later `ResourceMap::get_face(0, ...)` still trusts `get_resource_count() == 130`, dereferences the sanitized-zero `resourcesZ` as `Null(UnsizedArrayOf<ResourceRecord>)`, and obtains a zero-filled `ResourceRecord`. `ResourceRecord::get_face()` then interprets the zero-length data block at EOF as an `LArrayOf<HBUINT8>` header and casts its `.arrayZ` field to `OpenTypeFontFace`, placing the face pointer four bytes past EOF. `_hb_face_for_data_reference_table()` asks that forged face for `maxp`, and `OffsetTable::find_table_index()` reads `tables.len`; the underlying 16-bit big-endian load in `BEInt<unsigned short, 2>::operator unsigned short()` happens eight bytes beyond the 256-byte heap blob, matching the saved ASan trace. The fix makes dfont `resourcesZ`, `typeList`, `data`, and `map` non-nullable; in the staged witness, the concretely implicated field is the first `sfnt` `resourcesZ`, because `map=1`, `data=256`, and `typeList=14` are already nonzero on the observed path.

staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable snapshot. Its relevant dfont lines match the saved ASan stack, and relative to metadata vulnerable commit `01b9148d9ae7d18228538774243e49840cfd2499` the vulnerable dfont offset semantics are unchanged.

source.description: First non-harness project statement on the crashing path. It sanitizes the attacker blob as `OT::OpenTypeFontFile` and stores the resulting face closure that later lazy table lookups read from.
source.value_from: The exact staged `poc` is 256 bytes and begins `00 00 01 00 00 00 00 01 00 00 00 00 00 01 00 00`. When this call reinterprets the blob as `OT::OpenTypeFontFile`, those bytes become `DFontTag`, `data=256`, `map=1`, `dataLen=0`, and `mapLen=0x00010000`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The first `sfnt` type's resource-array offset is sanitized through a null-enabled `OffsetTo`, so when deep validation of the promised `130` `ResourceRecord`s fails, HarfBuzz rewrites `resourcesZ` to `0` and still accepts the blob instead of rejecting the malformed dfont.
root_cause.note: The staged fix changes this field from `OffsetTo<UnsizedArrayOf<ResourceRecord> >` to `OffsetTo<UnsizedArrayOf<ResourceRecord>, HBUINT16, false>`, preventing failed deep validation from collapsing into a nullable zero offset.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The big-endian 16-bit load of `OffsetTable.tables.len` reads from the forged `OpenTypeFontFace` header beyond the 256-byte sanitized blob.
sink.note: The saved Stage 01 crash summary is `SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow /src/harfbuzz/src/./hb-machinery.hh:655:13 in BEInt<unsigned short, 2>::operator unsigned short() const`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is where the first type record's attacker-controlled `tag` and `resCountM1` bytes become the concrete count `130` that is later paired with `resourcesZ=44` during deep resource-array validation.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: At `type_base = 15` in the exact staged witness, record 0 stores `tag='sfnt'`, `resCountM1=129`, and `resourcesZ=44`.

parser_admitted.description: The witness's first four bytes `0x00000100` are accepted as `DFontTag`, so top-level OpenType sanitization enters the dfont parser instead of rejecting the blob or taking the ordinary sfnt path.

maxp_requested.description: The saved crash stack reaches `_hb_face_for_data_reference_table()` from `load_num_glyphs()`, so the observed table lookup on the forged face is the `maxp` request performed before `hb_font_create()` finishes loading face metrics.

evidence_limitations: Runtime disambiguation is disabled in `run_flags.json`, so Stage 02 used only the staged source, patch, saved crash trace, and exact witness bytes. For this sample those artifacts close the dfont-specific chain without extra instrumentation.

Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image, so `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` remains `false` even though the staged patch text matches the specific nullable-`resourcesZ` obligation reconstructed here.

coarse_trace.summary: The 256-byte witness is sanitized as a dfont. Its header yields `map=1`, `data=256`, `typeList=14`, and the first `sfnt` resource-type record advertises `resCountM1=129` and `resourcesZ=44`.
Deep validation of the promised `130` `ResourceRecord`s fails, but the null-enabled `resourcesZ` field is neutered to `0`. Later the same type record is trusted during face lookup for index `0`.

Dereferencing the sanitized-zero `resourcesZ` returns a null resource array, yielding a zero-filled `ResourceRecord` whose zero data offset turns the zero-length data block at EOF into a forged `OpenTypeFontFace` starting four bytes past the blob.

The lazy `maxp` table lookup treats that forged face as an `OffsetTable`; reading `tables.len` overreads the sanitized heap blob, and `BEInt<unsigned short, 2>::operator unsigned short()` triggers the observed ASan crash.

fine_trace.note: Source. This is the first non-harness statement on the crashing path. It turns the 256-byte witness into a writable `OT::OpenTypeFontFile` for sanitization and stores the resulting face closure. The same blob begins with `0x00000100`, so the later top-level dispatch takes the dfont parser.
The first four witness bytes decode as `DFontTag`, so sanitization enters `ResourceForkHeader` instead of the normal sfnt or TTC handlers.

The dfont header bytes set `data = 256` and `dataLen = 0`. This succeeds and establishes `data_base = &(this+data)` at absolute file offset 256, a zero-length data block exactly at EOF. That EOF pointer is later reused as the base for `ResourceRecord::get_face()`.

With `map = 1` from the dfont header and `typeList = 14` from map bytes 25-26, this materializes `type_base` at absolute file offset 15. The `ArrayOfM1<ResourceTypeRecord>` there has `lenM1 = 1`, so the map exposes exactly two type records.

At `type_base`, record 0 stores `tag='sfnt'`, `resCountM1=129`, and `resourcesZ=44`. This line turns that record into `get_resource_count() == 130`, the count later used both for deep validation and for the later resource-array index check.

Root cause. For the first `sfnt` type, `resourcesZ = 44` points to absolute offset 59, where only 197 bytes remain. Deep validation would need `130 * 12 = 1560` bytes for the promised `ResourceRecord` array, so the child `UnsizedArrayOf<ResourceRecord>::sanitize(...)` fails. Because `resourcesZ` is declared as null-enabled `OffsetTo<UnsizedArrayOf<ResourceRecord> >`, `OffsetTo::sanitize()` takes its `|| neuter (c)` path and rewrites the field to `0` instead of rejecting the blob. The fix changes this declaration to `..., HBUINT16, false>` so the failure cannot collapse into a null offset.

Later, when `_hb_face_for_data_reference_table()` asks the dfont for face 0, this loop selects the same first type again because it is `sfnt` and `idx == 0 < 130`. Control therefore reaches `get_resource_record(0, type_base)` while still carrying the step-6-mutated `resourcesZ` and the EOF `data_base` from step 3.

Inside `type.get_resource_record(0, type_base)`, the step-6 zeroed `resourcesZ` is dereferenced. Because this offset type is still null-enabled at runtime, `operator()` returns `Null(UnsizedArrayOf<ResourceRecord>)` instead of interpreting `0` as a real in-structure offset.

The null array from step 8 is wrapped in `hb_array_t<ResourceRecord>` with `len = 130`, and `i = 0` stays in range. Indexing therefore returns the first zero-filled `ResourceRecord` from HarfBuzz's null pool instead of a record from the PoC.

The zero-filled `ResourceRecord` from step 9 has `offset = 0`, and this field is explicitly non-nullable (`OffsetTo<LArrayOf<HBUINT8>, HBUINT24, false>`). `data_base + offset` therefore resolves an `LArrayOf<HBUINT8>` header at the EOF pointer from step 3, and `.arrayZ` advances four bytes past that header. The resulting `OpenTypeFontFace` reference starts at absolute file offset 260, i.e. four bytes beyond the 256-byte blob.

fine_trace.code:
const OT::OpenTypeFontFace &ot_face = ot_file.get_face (data->index, &base_offset);

const OT::OpenTypeTable &table = ot_face.get_table_by_tag (tag);
fine_trace.note: When HarfBuzz later lazily resolves a table from this face closure, `ot_file.get_face(0, &base_offset)` returns the forged EOF+4 face from step 10. The saved crash stack shows this specific request came from `hb_face_t::load_num_glyphs()` via `reference_table<OT::maxp>`, so `tag` is `maxp` on the observed path.

The forged `ot_face` from step 11 is treated as an `OffsetTable`. To choose linear versus binary search, this line first converts `tables.len` from the `BinSearchHeader` at the start of that forged face, even though the header lies beyond the heap allocation.

fine_trace.code: inline operator uint32_t (void) const { return len; }
fine_trace.note: Evaluating `tables.len` at step 12 dispatches into this conversion and requests the first 16-bit field of the forged `BinSearchHeader` from step 10.

Sink. The big-endian 16-bit load for `len` reads from the forged face header starting at absolute file offset 264, which is eight bytes past the 256-byte writable blob allocated during sanitization. AddressSanitizer reports the observed `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` here.

poc.trigger: Use the exact staged 256-byte witness. Its dfont header decodes as `data=0x00000100`, `map=0x00000001`, `dataLen=0`, `mapLen=0x00010000`; `map+24` stores `typeList=0x000e`; and the first type record at `type_base=15` stores `tag='sfnt'`, `resCountM1=129`, and `resourcesZ=44`. Those exact fields make deep validation of the first resource array need `1560` bytes from absolute offset `59` while only `197` remain, so vulnerable sanitization neuters `resourcesZ` to `0` and the later `maxp` lookup crashes in `BEInt<unsigned short, 2>::operator unsigned short()`.

format.name: Apple dfont resource-fork blob for hb-shape-fuzzer
format.contract: Use the exact staged 256-byte witness. It must preserve the header bytes `00 00 01 00 00 00 00 01 00 00 00 00 00 01 00 00`, `typeList=0x000e`, and the first type record `tag='sfnt'`, `resCountM1=129`, `resourcesZ=44`. These exact values are sufficient to make `resourcesZ.sanitize()` rewrite the field to zero and to place the later forged `OpenTypeFontFace` four bytes past EOF, after which the `maxp` lookup reads `tables.len` from absolute file offset `264`.
